title: A decision‐support framework for sustainable selection of ethanol–gasoline additive formulations considering combustion, performance, and emission trade‐offs
content:
Abstract

Ethanol–gasoline blends are increasingly adopted to meet emission regulations and reduce dependence on fossil fuels; however, their application is constrained by low calorific value, high latent heat of vaporization, and poor cold-start performance. This study presents an AHP–TOPSIS methodology for preliminary screening and ranking of fuel additives considering thermophysical, combustion, and regulatory criteria. Eight criteria were considered: Research Octane Number (RON), calorific value, oxygen content, latent heat of vaporization, density, vapor pressure, viscosity, and laminar flame speed. Twelve additives were evaluated using the proposed framework. AHP results indicate that RON (0.308) and vapor pressure (0.259) received the highest weights, highlighting their importance for knock resistance, combustion behavior, fuel vaporization, and cold-start performance. TOPSIS identified diethyl ether (DEE) as the highest-ranked candidate, with a closeness coefficient of 0.904, followed by acetone (0.537) and MTBE (0.516). Sensitivity analysis over the weight range of 0.20–0.80 revealed criterion-dependent rank changes, with substantial sensitivity associated with calorific value, oxygen content, and vapor pressure. DEE, acetone, and MTBE were subsequently experimentally evaluated at 5% concentration in E20 under cold-start and full-throttle conditions. DEE demonstrated favorable performance characteristics, including higher torque, brake power, and brake thermal efficiency than E20, together with substantial reductions in cold-start HC and NOx emissions. However, its full-throttle emission response was parameter dependent. Therefore, the AHP–TOPSIS results represent a screening outcome requiring blend-specific optimization and experimental validation. The framework provides a systematic basis for prioritizing candidate additives for further investigation and sustainable ethanol–gasoline fuel formulation.
